files.content:
import random
from people import Child, NaughtyChild, NiceChild


class Santa:
   #Base class for Santas. Each santa has an age and an experience, and also a sack with gifts.
   def __init__(self, age, experience):
      self.age = age
      self.experience = experience
      self.sack = ["Doll", "Train", "Ball", "Book"]
   
   def __str__(self):
      return f"{self.age} years old Santa with experience level {self.experience}"
   
   def deliver(self, toPerson):
      toPerson.receive(random.choice(self.sack))



class SeniorSanta(Santa):
   #Child class - Senior santa has earned himself a name and a rank, and is somewhat more strategic when he delivers packages...
   def __init__(self, age, experience, rank, name):
      super().__init__(age, experience)
      self.rank = rank
      self.name = name
   
   def __str__(self):
      return f"Senior santa {self.name} with rank {self.rank}"
   
   def deliver(self, toPerson):
      if toPerson.isNaughty():
         toPerson.receive("Lump of coal")
      else:
         wantedgifts = set(self.sack).intersection(set(toPerson.getWishlist()))
         toPerson.receive(random.choice(list(wantedgifts)))
      print("Hohoho")

if __name__ == "__main__":
   '''Test code for Santas. Requires other people as well. Does not run on import.'''
   testSanta = Santa(45, 4)
   senior = SeniorSanta(89, 100, "expert", "Nicholas")
   child1 = NaughtyChild("Tom")
   child2 = NiceChild("Tage")
         
   print(senior)
   print(child1.getWishlist())
   senior.deliver(child1)
   senior.deliver(child2)

   print(testSanta)
   testSanta.deliver(child1)
   testSanta.deliver(child2)
